A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe the same Visual CounterFact dataset and Pixels Versus Priors steering study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across layout changes and the removal of Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on three multimodal models, including task accuracies, early-decoding statistics, steering success rates, attention analyses, and PCA results.

after.justification: v2 reports original experimental results in Tables 1–3 and the main-text and appendix analyses, including revised steering results and a new attention case study.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 retains the same procedure: average differences between final-text-token MLP activations under contrasting prompts, then add the resulting vectors across selected layers. No new algorithmic component is introduced. The contradictory vector label in the revised schematic does not establish an actual procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same color and relative-size tasks and 2,904-image Visual CounterFact dataset: 575 original and 575 counterfactual color images, plus 877 original and 877 counterfactual size images. The attention example does not introduce distinct task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Both evaluate LLaVA-Next-7B, Qwen2-VL-7B, and Janus-Pro-7B, retaining unsteered predictions and prompt changes as comparison conditions. No evaluated comparator is added or removed; reverse-direction attention comparisons expanded in the main text already appeared in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes the operational flip criterion from simply exceeding the alternative to exceeding it by at least 5%. Table 3 revises the reported intervention windows, such as LLaVA color WK-to-CF changing from layers 16–19 to 14–16. These are refinements within retained experiments; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 6 replaces the LLaVA PCA analysis with a before-and-after token/image attention case study. Appendix E's PCA discussion is removed, although Figure 9 retains the other models' PCA plots. Early-decoding and aggregate attention analyses remain, so this is a limited change in supplementary analysis rather than a new validation program.

E5.justification: The statistical reporting practice is unchanged. Both retain the same shaded early-decoding plots, without adding run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Central numerical evidence is extensively revised in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5, 10, and 11. For example, Table 1's LLaVA color CF-plus-most accuracy changes from 37.91% to 47.26%, while Table 3's color WK-to-CF rates change from 89.9/93.6/94.0% to 99.5/99.7/98.6% across the three models. Changed flip criteria and intervention windows prevent treating all revisions as comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4.2's mathematics is retained apart from hats marking intervened states. However, v2 Figure 3 newly labels mean(h_this − h_most) as S_WK, contradicting both versions' equation S_WK = mean(h_most − h_this). This introduces a sign inconsistency in the mathematical specification; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the quantitative steering claim from average color/size success of 92.5%/74.6% to 99.3%/80.8%. The central contributions—Visual CounterFact, mid-to-late visual override, and bidirectional activation steering—retain the same scope.

C2.justification: v2 removes the PCA-based explanation of asymmetric representational reorientation from Section 5.3 and Appendix E. Section 5.4 instead adds an interpretation of the attention example as shifting focus from text to image regions. The broader visual-dominance interpretation and Section 7 limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 3 reports revised intervention-layer settings. Removing Appendix E also removes the explicit description that the retained PCA analysis projects the final hidden state of the last text token. Dataset-generation instructions and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work discussion are unchanged in substance. Both versions position the dataset and steering approach against the same counterfactual benchmarks, multimodal editing methods, and activation-steering research.

P1.justification: Most prose, terminology, and section ordering are retained. Local edits remove the redundant Appendix A overview and PCA discussion, add an attention-example explanation, and update numerical statements. This is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially reorganized: Figure 3 becomes a two-panel construction/intervention schematic, Figure 5 expands from two to four panels, and Figure 6 is replaced. Tables 1 and 2 become full-width comparisons, Figures 10–11 are redrawn and reordered, and Figure 1 is enlarged. These changes exceed simple numerical updates or repagination.

improvement.justification: Clearer layouts and an explicit flip threshold help, but v2 introduces inconsistencies absent in v1. Section 5.2 retains flip means 1.24/0.79 while Table 2 now reports 1.31/0.84. Figure 5's attention-mass change peaks near 0.23, while Section 5.4 and Appendix Table 5 retain 40%. Figure 3 also introduces the S_WK sign conflict. These errors weaken reporting reliability and outweigh the limited presentation benefits; higher reported scores alone do not establish improved quality.
